analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | Europe reads | JBHT | AER 16 Oct 2026
key_insights: Futures edged higher Friday as comments from Chair Warsh shifted the market tone on future rate cuts. Overnight, KOSPI rose 2.05% and Japan 1.39%. Most of Europe was strong and the UK was the lone market lower.

Commodities and rates: Brent $106, WTI $97, both down very modestly. European natural gas (TTF) reached $88, up two-fold this year. The 10-year yield is 5.10%, holding yesterday's reversal. DXY is below 102 and Bitcoin is flat at $82k.

Global systematic L/S funds fell 1.4% on Thursday, nearly a 4 standard deviation move. The desk says the move was about gross exposure rather than net exposure, with multiple-standard-deviation squeezes in shorts alongside equally violent declines in longs, including through the European session. The desk reads this as aggressive de-grossing and expects choppy trading.

The desk is increasingly optimistic that a level has been found where much of the concern is priced into semis. It wonders whether selling hyperscalers versus semis becomes the relative trade. It sees the AI spending demand picture as excellent, but financing and electrification bottlenecks remain real.

Oil remains stubbornly high and the desk says US political events make geopolitical risk increasingly difficult to ignore. It is watching the QRA questionnaire and US HY spreads, which found their feet on Thursday.

Schneider Electric Q3 beat and raise: sales beat by 3% with 17% organic growth. EM and IA beat expectations on China and North America, data center was up triple digits, and guidance was raised 1 point on growth and 20-30bps on margins. The stock was down modestly on concerns tied to the PTC acquisition. The desk expects low single digit consensus revisions.

JBHT Q3 EPS was $1.82 vs $1.82 consensus on revenue of $3.680bn vs $3.585bn consensus. EBIT was $247mm, essentially in line. The desk's takeaway from the call: operating leverage is slow to develop, price and volume do not move together (pricing somewhat better in Q3, volumes worse), and Dedicated takes a step back before it benefits. Feedback skews cautious but mixed. The implied move was 5%.

JBHT segments: Intermodal revenue $1.83bn (+20% y/y, in line), EBIT $148mm vs $147mm consensus, volume +8% (Eastern network +18%), revenue per load ex fuel +2%. Dedicated revenue $960mm vs $945mm consensus, but EBIT $82mm vs $92.5mm consensus. ICS revenue $434mm vs $393mm consensus, EBIT $9.6mm vs $3mm, volume +22%, revenue per load +29%. FMS revenue $200mm vs $196mm, EBIT $1.6mm vs $5mm. Truck revenue $261mm vs $246mm, EBIT $7mm vs break-even.

GS Equity Research (Catie) raised its AerCap (AER) 3Q26 EPS ex-purchase accounting estimate to $5.00 from $4.30, vs FactSet consensus of $4.44, on a much higher gain-on-sales forecast. The company's transaction report showed 85 asset sales (70 from its owned portfolio), with 52 owned aircraft sold vs GSe 29. Higher gains are partly offset by lower rental revenue and an updated interest expense outlook.

GSe raised AER FY26 EPS ex-purchase accounting to $19.65 from $19.50, vs consensus $18.99. It expects a 3Q beat and a raise of the FY26 outlook for the third consecutive quarter. GSe forecasts EPS ex-gains of $14.41 vs company guidance of $14.00. It lowers 4Q26 gain on sales because it now assumes most 2H26 sales occur in 3Q.

On AER, investors will focus on gain on sale margin and net spread. GS expects a similar gain on sale margin, helped by engine, widebody and current-tech asset sales. It expects a sequential decline in net spread from a high level of sales and the timing of the roll-off of low-priced debt. It expects a material step-up in net spread in 4Q26 and beyond as new aircraft with higher lease rates deliver, COVID-era leases are marked to market, and grounded aircraft return to service.
FBIN will sell its Fiberon business to Inteplast for $160mm, which the desk calls a small but well thought out catalyst. TSLA was higher pre-market on the roadster reveal.

Earnings pick up next week. Names in focus early in the week: GE, GM, MMM, NOC, RTX, UAL, CSX, ESI, PKG, KNX, URI. Investor questions so far cover PCAR TP&O gross margins, NVT orders, MMM organic growth, and EMR, ROK, JCI and WWD guides.
